[id="extensions-langchain4j-ingest-usage"]
== Usage
[id="extensions-langchain4j-ingest-usage-ingesting-a-directory"]
=== Ingesting a directory

Point a pipeline at a folder and the files in it become a knowledge base. No route, no ingestion code:

[source,properties]
----
quarkus.camel.ai.ingest.products.source.directory=/var/data/product-docs
quarkus.camel.ai.ingest.products.embedding-store=products
quarkus.camel.ai.ingest.products.embedding-model=my-model
----

Documents are read as text — there is no format parsing, so a PDF or DOCX must be converted before it reaches a pipeline. Each file is read as UTF-8, split into overlapping segments (`max-segment-size` and `max-overlap-size`), embedded and written to the store. `embedding-store` and `embedding-model` name CDI beans and may be omitted when the application has exactly one of each; with several, naming one is required rather than guessed.

Every segment carries `camel_quarkus_pipeline` and `camel_quarkus_document_id` metadata, so retrieval can cite which document an answer came from.

[NOTE]
====
This preview ingests what it is given and keeps no record of it, so a document ingested twice leaves two copies in the store. That has consequences worth planning around: a restart re-reads the whole directory, because the file consumer's duplicate protection is an in-memory register capped at 1000 entries rather than a persisted one; and a polled consumer such as `aws2-s3` with `deleteAfterRead(false)` re-reads every object on every poll, growing the store without bound. Ingest into a store you can rebuild, or keep the polling interval long, until the synchronising engine lands. Keeping a store in step with a changing source — skipping unchanged documents, replacing edited ones and removing deleted ones — needs that record, and arrives in a later release.
====

[id="extensions-langchain4j-ingest-usage-any-other-source"]
=== Any other source

Beyond a directory, a pipeline reads from any Camel consumer at all — the roughly 300 components, with their own option names, their own defaults and their own documentation. The way to reach them is the Endpoint DSL, so the options are typed rather than spelled into a URI:

[source,java]
----
@Ingest("product-docs")
IngestPipeline productDocs() {
    return IngestPipeline.from(Source.endpoint(dsl -> dsl.aws2S3("product-docs")
            .region("eu-west-1")
            .deleteAfterRead(false))
            .documentId("CamelAwsS3Key"))
            .embeddingStore("products");
}
----

Nothing is imported: typing `dsl.` lists a factory for every Camel component, and each completes its own options. `Source.endpoint(aws2S3(...))` with a static import of `StaticEndpointBuilders` is the same DSL for those who prefer it.

Ingestion needs a stable id per document, and where that id lives is the consumer's business: the object key for S3 (`CamelAwsS3Key`), the record key for Kafka (`CamelKafkaKey`), a header your own route sets. `documentId` names it. Without it, the pipeline expects the `CamelIngestDocumentId` header and fails the exchange when it is absent.

Setting `source.uri` is what makes a pipeline consume from a component rather than read a directory — there is no source type to declare. The URI is build-time by design — a runtime-overridable consumer URI would be arbitrary component invocation. Property placeholders inside it still resolve at startup, so credentials and endpoints stay runtime configuration:

[source,properties]
----
quarkus.camel.ai.ingest.custom.source.uri=direct:custom-source
quarkus.camel.ai.ingest.custom.source.document-id=CamelAwsS3Key
----

Give `document-id` a header name, or a full simple-language expression when the id is not a plain header — though in a properties file `${...}` is expanded by MicroProfile Config before Camel sees it, so the bare header name is the form to prefer there.
[id="extensions-langchain4j-ingest-usage-declaring-a-pipeline-in-java"]
=== Declaring a pipeline in Java

Every property has a builder twin, for those who prefer IDE completion to property names:

[source,java]
----
@Ingest("datasheets")
IngestPipeline datasheets() {
    return IngestPipeline.from(Source.endpoint(dsl -> dsl.aws2S3("product-docs").region("eu-west-1"))
                    .documentId("CamelAwsS3Key"))
            .embeddingStore("products")
            .splitter(500, 50);
}
----

`Source` offers the same source three ways, and the lambda above is the one to reach for: `dsl.` lists a factory for every Camel component and each completes its own options, with nothing to import and nothing to look up. `Source.endpoint(aws2S3(...))` is the identical DSL through a static import of `StaticEndpointBuilders`, and `Source.endpoint("aws2-s3://…")` takes a raw URI for the cases where one is assembled at runtime. `Source.file` is the shorthand for a directory, and `.documentId(...)` names the id in every case.

Sharp edge worth knowing about the first two: the DSL factories all ship in one artifact, so the call compiles even when the connector extension is absent — the missing component is then reported at startup.

`@Ingest` methods must return `IngestPipeline`, take no parameters and carry a name that no configuration-declared pipeline already uses — all three are build failures otherwise.


[id="extensions-langchain4j-ingest-quarkus-langchain4j-bom"]
== LangChain4j usage

=== Dependency management

In order to ensure alignment across all Quarkus and LangChain4j related dependencies, it is recommended to import the LangChain4j BOM as below:
[source,xml,subs=attributes+]
----
<dependencyManagement>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>dev.langchain4j</groupId>
      <artifactId>langchain4j-bom</artifactId>
      <version>{langchain4j-version}</version>
      <type>pom</type>
      <scope>import</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
  ...
</dependencyManagement>
----

Note that the import order is paramount when using maven `dependencyManagement`.
As such, one might need to import the `langchain4j-bom` before other related Camel and Quarkus BOMs.

=== Quarkus LangChain4j support

WARNING: At present, this extension is neither tested with nor intended to be used in conjunction with any Quarkus LangChain4j extensions.
Consequently, both JVM and native modes may exhibit unexpected behaviour or fail to function correctly in such configurations.

| Configuration property | Type | Default


a|icon:lock[title=Fixed at build time] [[quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-source-uri]]`link:#quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-source-uri[quarkus.camel.ai.ingest."pipeline-name".source.uri]`

The Camel consumer URI feeding this pipeline: any component, with its own options.
Setting it is what makes the pipeline consume from that component. Leaving it unset
makes the pipeline read a directory instead, named by the runtime property
{@code quarkus.camel.ai.ingest.<name>.source.directory} — see
{@link IngestRunTimeConfig.PipelineRunTimeConfig.SourceRunTimeConfig#directory()}.

<p>
Build-time by design: a runtime-overridable consumer URI would be arbitrary
component invocation. Property placeholders inside it still resolve at startup, so
credentials and endpoints remain runtime configuration.
| `string`
| 

a|icon:lock[title=Fixed at build time] [[quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-embedding-store]]`link:#quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-embedding-store[quarkus.camel.ai.ingest."pipeline-name".embedding-store]`

Name of the {@code EmbeddingStore} bean to write to. When not set, the only one present
is used.
| `string`
| 

a|icon:lock[title=Fixed at build time] [[quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-embedding-model]]`link:#quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-embedding-model[quarkus.camel.ai.ingest."pipeline-name".embedding-model]`

Name of the {@code EmbeddingModel} bean to embed with. When not set, the only one
present is used.
| `string`
| 

a|icon:lock[title=Fixed at build time] [[quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-max-segment-size]]`link:#quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-max-segment-size[quarkus.camel.ai.ingest."pipeline-name".max-segment-size]`

Maximum size of one segment, in characters.
| `int`
| `500`

a|icon:lock[title=Fixed at build time] [[quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-max-overlap-size]]`link:#quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-max-overlap-size[quarkus.camel.ai.ingest."pipeline-name".max-overlap-size]`

How much of the previous segment each segment repeats, in characters. Overlap keeps a
sentence split across a boundary retrievable from either side.
| `int`
| `50`

a| [[quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-enabled]]`link:#quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-enabled[quarkus.camel.ai.ingest."pipeline-name".enabled]`

Whether this pipeline starts. Useful to switch ingestion off in dev mode.
| `boolean`
| `true`

a| [[quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-source-directory]]`link:#quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-source-directory[quarkus.camel.ai.ingest."pipeline-name".source.directory]`

The directory to ingest documents from, for a pipeline that has no
{@code source.uri} — see
{@link IngestBuildTimeConfig.PipelineBuildTimeConfig.SourceBuildTimeConfig#uri()}.
A path is a deployment concern, so unlike the URI it stays runtime configuration.
Setting both is an error.

| 

a| [[quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-source-recursive]]`link:#quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-source-recursive[quarkus.camel.ai.ingest."pipeline-name".source.recursive]`

Whether subdirectories are ingested too, when reading a directory.
| `boolean`
| `true`

a| [[quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-source-document-id]]`link:#quarkus-camel-ai-ingest-pipeline-name-source-document-id[quarkus.camel.ai.ingest."pipeline-name".source.document-id]`

Where the document id lives in the exchange the consumer delivers: normally the
name of a header, such as {@code CamelAwsS3Key} for an S3 consumer or
{@code CamelKafkaKey} for a Kafka one. A value containing {@code ${...}} is taken
as a simple-language expression instead, for ids that are not a plain header —
though in a properties file MicroProfile Config expands such a value before Camel
sees it, so the header name is the form to prefer there.

<p>
When not set, a pipeline reading a directory uses the file name, and one consuming
from a component uses the {@code CamelIngestDocumentId} header.
